road.name: Touchet Road / FR-64 (Bluewood Road) from Dayton
road.status: Paved North Touchet Road out of Dayton becomes gravel-to-dirt Forest Service Road 64 at the forest boundary as it climbs toward the Bluewood ski area; the climbing dikes sit right along this road roughly 16-17 miles in (about 1-2 miles past the Middle Point Ridge Trailhead). Approach paths to individual crags (Megadike, Minidike, Weeping Wall, Joe's Rock) are unofficial, brushy, and easy to lose.
road.driveNote: Roughly 25-30 minutes (about 20 miles) from Dayton, WA via S 4th Street/North Touchet Road (FR-64).
road.seasonalGate: FR-64 continues past The Dikes to Ski Bluewood and is the ski area's only road, so it stays in use through winter; snow on the crags and approach slopes, rather than the road, limits climbing to roughly May through October, sometimes from April.

_raw.special_hazards: Climbing rock (check current condition via climbing guides)
_raw.permit_cost_structure: Day use only; NW Forest Pass $5 (5-day) or $30 (annual)

access.fees: Day use only; NW Forest Pass $5 (5-day) or $30 (annual)
access.notes: A basalt "cordwood-jointed" dike/fin formation in the East Fork Touchet River valley off FS Rd 64, ~16-17 mi south of Dayton, WA. Unmaintained approach, seasonally snowed in late fall through spring.

road.name: Touchet Road / FR-64 (Bluewood Road) from Dayton
road.status: Paved North Touchet Road out of Dayton becomes gravel-to-dirt Forest Service Road 64 at the forest boundary as it climbs toward the Bluewood ski area; the climbing dikes sit right along this road roughly 16-17 miles in (about 1-2 miles past the Middle Point Ridge Trailhead). Approach paths to individual crags (Megadike, Minidike, Weeping Wall, Joe's Rock) are unofficial, brushy, and easy to lose.
road.driveNote: Roughly 25-30 minutes (about 20 miles) from Dayton, WA via S 4th Street/North Touchet Road (FR-64).
road.seasonalGate: FR-64 continues past The Dikes to Ski Bluewood and is the ski area's only road, so it stays in use through winter; snow on the crags and approach slopes, rather than the road, limits climbing to roughly May through October, sometimes from April.
